_meta.indication: NATPARA is a parathyroid hormone indicated as an adjunct to calcium and vitamin D to control hypocalcemia in patients with hypoparathyroidism.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 24-week study; subjects randomized 2:1 to NPSP558 or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 to 85 years with history of hypoparathyroidism for ≥ 18 months requiring vitamin D metabolite/analog therapy
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of responders at Week 24 — a composite requiring ≥50% reduction from baseline oral calcium dose AND ≥50% reduction from baseline active vitamin D dose AND an albumin-corrected total serum calcium that was maintained or normalized (≥7.5 mg/dL) and did not exceed the upper limit of normal
pivotal_trials.result: Responder rate 46 (55%) with Natpara vs 1 (3%) with placebo; p<.0001

nct_ctgov.title: Use of NPSP558 in the Treatment of Hypoparathyroidism

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%): paresthesia, hypocalcemia, headache, hypercalcemia, nausea, hypoaesthesia, diarrhea, vomiting, arthralgia, and pain in extremity. Severe hypercalcemia (in pivotal trial, 2 patients on NATPARA required IV fluids) and severe hypocalcemia (highest risk when NATPARA is withheld, missed or abruptly discontinued) have been reported.
target_moa: Parathyroid hormone (rhPTH[1-84]) replacement; raises serum calcium by increasing renal tubular calcium reabsorption, increasing intestinal calcium absorption (via conversion of 25 OH vitamin D to 1,25 OH2 vitamin D), and increasing bone turnover that releases calcium into the circulation.
modality: peptide (recombinant full-length human parathyroid hormone, rhPTH[1-84])

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: POTENTIAL RISK OF OSTEOSARCOMA — in male and female rats, parathyroid hormone caused a dose- and treatment-duration-dependent increase in the incidence of osteosarcoma (a malignant bone tumor); a risk to humans could not be excluded. Because of this risk, prescribe NATPARA only to patients who cannot be well-controlled on calcium and active vitamin D.

rems.type: Because of the potential risk of osteosarcoma, NATPARA is available only through a restricted REMS program (NATPARA REMS Program) under which only certified healthcare providers can prescribe and only certified pharmacies can dispense NATPARA; ETASU include prescriber and pharmacy certification and documentation of safe use conditions.

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory committee met September 12, 2014; voted Yes=8, No=5, Abstain=0 that the data supported approval of Natpara for the long-term treatment of hypoparathyroidism.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug Designation granted in 2007 for NPSP558 (rhPTH[1-84]) for hypoparathyroidism.

citations.quote: In 2007, the Agency granted Orphan Drug Designation for NPSP558 for hypoparathyroidism. A pre-IND meeting was held on December 17, 2007. The Applicant submitted IND 76,514 on September 19, 2008 with the initiation of the Phase 3 pivotal trial CL1-11040 for the hypoparathyroidism indication.

summary.text: NATPARA (rhPTH[1-84]) received traditional/full approval under a standard review as a BLA, based on the single pivotal placebo-controlled trial REPLACE whose primary composite responder endpoint was met. It had received Orphan Drug Designation for hypoparathyroidism in 2007, was presented at an advisory committee (September 12, 2014; vote 8-5), and was approved with a REMS and multiple post-marketing requirements to address the potential osteosarcoma and hypercalcemia risks.

citations.quote: The Applicant conducted one pivotal trial and three supportive trials. The Applicant met the primary endpoint in the pivotal trial. Approximately 55% of subjects taking Natpara® reduced the amounts of calcium and vitamin D analogs by 50%, while maintaining a normal serum calcium level. In 2007, the Agency granted Orphan Drug Designation for NPSP558 for hypoparathyroidism. A pre-IND meeting was held on December 17, 2007. The Applicant submitted IND 76,514 on September 19, 2008 with the initiation of the Phase 3 pivotal trial CL1-11040 for the hypoparathyroidism indication.
In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Natpara to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the potential risk of osteosarcoma.

requirement.text: 2856-1: A study in Fischer 344 rats to ascertain the effect of different Natpara dosing regimens on osteoblast proliferation, as an indicator of relative osteosarcoma risk.

citations.quote: 2856-1 A study in Fischer 344 rats to ascertain the effect of different Natpara (parathyroid hormone) dosing regimens on osteoblast proliferation, as an indicator of relative osteosarcoma risk.

requirement.text: 2856-2: An enhanced pharmacovigilance study of osteosarcoma in patients with hypoparathyroidism treated with Natpara, including reports of osteosarcoma for a period of 15 years from the date of approval.

citations.quote: 2856-2 An enhanced pharmacovigilance study of osteosarcoma in patients with hypoparathyroidism treated with Natpara (parathyroid hormone). The study will include reports of osteosarcoma for a period of 15 years from the date of approval, and will include assessment and analysis of spontaneous reports of osteosarcoma in patients treated with Natpara (parathyroid hormone), with specialized follow-up to collect additional information on these cases.

requirement.text: 2856-3: A clinical pharmacology trial to assess the PK and PD effects of Natpara dose and dosing regimen on the control of serum calcium and normalization of urinary calcium excretion.

citations.quote: 2856-3 A clinical pharmacology trial to assess the pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamic effects (PD) of Natpara (parathyroid hormone) dose and dosing regimen on the control of serum calcium and normalization of calcium excretion in urine. Modeling and simulation using mechanistic model-based assessment of prior PK/PD data should be used to design this trial.
